claims.claim: AMC is a portable skill with progressive enforcement, not a harness, hosted coordinator, daemon or graph framework.
claims.source_supported_fact: Skills are folders of instructions plus optional scripts. Claude Code Projects is a hosted coordinator with cloud threads.
claims.architectural_inference: Keep AMC installable as a skill. Ship an optional checker. Do not copy Projects infrastructure.
claims.does_not_prove: That a skill outperforms a hosted coordinator.

claims.claim: Direct work is the default for tightly coupled work, a strong lead and high coordination cost. Delegation is for decomposable work or a separate specialist context.
claims.source_supported_fact: Kim et al. found the single-agent baseline predicted whether coordination helped. Decomposability mattered more than complexity. Artificial splits often hurt. SWE-bench MAS variants slightly degraded on a 20-instance subset per cell.
claims.architectural_inference: AMC uses a cautious direct default. That is not a theorem that sequential work is always best, and it does not by itself validate sequential specialists.
claims.does_not_prove: A universal sequential rule for all coding agents, or that AMC specialists beat a strong single session.

claims.claim: A worker receives a short goal, scope, facts, file pointers and acceptance checks. The repository may still be available.
claims.source_supported_fact: Anthropic recommends high-signal context and just-in-time retrieval.
claims.architectural_inference: Packets limit injected emphasis. They do not hide the repo.
claims.does_not_prove: Packets improve every model or task.

claims.claim: A cloned or mounted repository is workspace availability, not proof that every file is in the active model context.
claims.source_supported_fact: Projects threads clone project repositories and start with instructions plus MEMORY.md. Other memory files open on demand. Threads compact automatically.
claims.architectural_inference: Distinguish accessible workspace, standing instructions, memory index, on-demand files, packet content and active context.
claims.does_not_prove: That Projects and AMC packets are equivalent.

claims.claim: The local Cursor cache observed on 2026-09-19 is Superpowers v6.1.1. That is installed state, not upstream.
claims.source_supported_fact: plugin.json in the local cache reports version 6.1.1 with SessionStart hooks.

claims.claim: Audited upstream snapshot v6.4.1 includes Native/inline plan execution, a choice versus subagent-driven development, one fresh whole-branch review at the end, and worktree isolation that can degrade with disclosure.
claims.source_supported_fact: Release v6.4.1 (commit 5bf4e78, 2026-09-19). executing-plans is Native mode: same session, no implementer/reviewer per task, task-done runs tests and writes the ledger only on success. using-git-worktrees tries native isolation, then git worktree, then continues in place if consent is refused or the sandbox blocks creation.
claims.architectural_inference: AMC differs as a small adaptive control policy, not as 'direct vs always-subagent'. Superpowers is a larger development-method suite. Invocation is instruction-controlled; scripts can be deterministic when run; isolation is host-dependent.
claims.does_not_prove: That Superpowers or AMC is better. Do not describe v6.4.1 as mandatory SDD.

claims.claim: Offline skill optimization needs a frozen target, bounded edits, held-out selection and accept-only-if-better.
claims.source_supported_fact: SkillOpt studies controlled add/delete/replace edits to a skill under a frozen agent setup, with held-out selection and rejected proposals.
claims.architectural_inference: AMC learning stays offline. No mid-run skill rewrite.
claims.does_not_prove: That skills are generally harmful, or that AMC should self-modify.

claims.claim: A relevant-looking skill can still reduce quality or efficiency, especially when optional procedure becomes mandatory ceremony.
claims.source_supported_fact: arXiv:2608.11888 attributes 307 skill-induced failures. Excessive procedure dominates efficiency regressions (114/182), mainly excessive verification (67) and heavy implementation pipelines (30).
claims.architectural_inference: Do not require a mission JSON or checker on trivial direct tasks.
claims.does_not_prove: That AMC's current skill is the right size, or that AMC causes those regressions.

claims.claim: The installed skill may include a stdlib checker. Running it is bundled_checker_enforced. Not running it is instruction_only.
claims.source_supported_fact: The official skill format allows optional scripts/ for deterministic work.
claims.architectural_inference: Ship scripts/amc-check.py. Do not create a daemon. If the host cannot run it, do not pretend it ran.
claims.does_not_prove: That users will invoke the checker, or that a checked receipt means better code.

claims.claim: Workers default to delegation_authority false. Reviewers and verifiers are read-only. Unauthorized nested delegation is a structured deviation when the checker runs.
claims.source_supported_fact: Hosts can spawn children. A skill cannot prevent that unless the host enforces it.
claims.architectural_inference: Detect nested delegation in the receipt. Record host auto-coordination as observed, not as the planned AMC route.

claims.claim: Optimizer loops are in scope only with a frozen evaluator, bounded surface and keep/discard rule.
claims.source_supported_fact: AVO commits if correct and not worse. autoresearch uses one metric and keep/discard.

claims.claim: AMC does not claim general superiority in quality, price, speed or autonomy versus direct work, Superpowers, Projects or other orchestrators.
claims.source_supported_fact: No AMC production outcome study exists in this repository.
claims.does_not_prove: That the option to delegate is useless.

claims.claim: Claude Code Projects is an execution substrate and hosted coordinator. AMC is a workflow policy that could run inside it. They are not the same product class.
claims.source_supported_fact: A project conversation routes work to cloud Claude Code threads with VM isolation, own branches, project memory and a 200-thread/day cap.
claims.architectural_inference: Do not copy that runtime. Two workflow policies should not silently own the same task.
